description: Option C answered affirmatively but not as posed. The 1/u^3 amplification is COMMON-MODE across the two anchors and cancels in the difference: dc_3/dQ_beta = 2.069e6 per MeV at each anchor, but d(swing)/dQ_beta = -1.241, a 1.67e6 cancellation. So the c_3 SLOPE is known to 15.41 ppm while its VALUE is 60.99% uncertain — 39576x sharper. CRITICAL LIMITATION: c_3(q) is completely determined once Q_beta^exp is fixed, so dc_3/dq is a computation from the extractor, not a measurement; the sharpness comes from experiment CANCELLING. The slope therefore tests a candidate derived c_3(q) against the framework's own ladder shape — theory against theory — and does NOT lift the precision block. Its value is as a FIT-DETECTOR: a one-anchor fit passes the 61%-slack value check trivially but cannot pass the 15 ppm slope check by accident. Complements registry section 9e, which correctly calls the swing a non-independent derivation TARGET; this distinguishes that from its use as a test OBSERVABLE. Scope-(a); no claim about (H1).
tier: error propagation on committed values (no fit)
